root_cause.text: batman-adv failed to tie tp_meter session lifetime to the mesh interface lifetime, leaving bat_priv->tp_list sessions and sender threads active while batadv_mesh_free() tore down the mesh, causing concurrent use of a shutting-down bat_priv.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that “TP meter sessions remain linked on bat_priv->tp_list” and that “batadv_mesh_free() currently tears down the mesh without first draining these sessions,” and the fix adds batadv_tp_stop_all(bat_priv) in batadv_mesh_free() plus completion-based waiting for sender thread exit before teardown continues.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop all TP activity during mesh teardown to ensure cleanup completes without lingering throughput meter operations.
intent_record.what: A call to batadv_tp_stop_all(bat_priv) was added in batadv_mesh_free(struct net_device *mesh_iface) immediately after batadv_purge_outstanding_packets(bat_priv, NULL) and before batadv_gw_node_free(bat_priv).
intent_record.how: When a mesh interface is being freed, the code now explicitly stops all throughput meter sessions or related TP activity for that mesh instance before continuing resource cleanup, preventing TP-related processing from persisting during teardown.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the completion header so the file can correctly use completion synchronization APIs during compilation.
intent_record.what: A single header include was added: `#include <linux/completion.h>` alongside the existing Linux kernel includes.
intent_record.how: This makes completion-related declarations and APIs available to this translation unit, allowing the file to compile if it uses completion synchronization primitives; by itself, it does not change runtime behavior unless needed to resolve previously missing declarations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent double-detach and cleanup races in TP sender teardown by making list removal idempotent and synchronously cancelling delayed work.
intent_record.what: The cleanup logic was split by extracting list removal and reference/count dropping from batadv_tp_sender_cleanup() into a new helper batadv_tp_list_detach(struct batadv_tp_vars *tp_vars). The new helper takes only tp_vars, checks hlist_unhashed(&tp_vars->list) under tp_list_lock, uses hlist_del_init_rcu() instead of hlist_del_rcu(), tracks whether detachment happened with a local boolean, and only then decrements tp_num and calls batadv_tp_vars_put(). The sender cleanup function signature was changed to remove the bat_priv parameter, its delayed work cancellation was changed from cancel_delayed_work() to cancel_delayed_work_sync(), and it now calls batadv_tp_list_detach(tp_vars) before deleting the timer.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the session is now detached from the mesh TP session list at most once, preventing duplicate list deletion, duplicate reference release, and duplicate tp_num decrement if cleanup paths race or repeat. Initializing the hlist node after deletion also makes later checks reliable. Using synchronous delayed-work cancellation ensures finish_work is no longer running before cleanup proceeds, avoiding concurrent access to the same session data during timer/list teardown.

intent_record.intent_summary: Signal sender-thread completion after cleanup and before releasing tp_vars, while updating the cleanup call to its new signature.
intent_record.what: The call to batadv_tp_sender_cleanup() was changed to remove the bat_priv argument and now passes only tp_vars, and a new complete(&tp_vars->finished) call was inserted immediately afterward before batadv_tp_vars_put(tp_vars).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the sender cleanup path now uses the updated cleanup function signature and explicitly signals completion on tp_vars->finished before dropping the tp_vars reference, allowing any waiter on that completion to be notified that the sender thread has fully finished its work.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the kthread startup failure path by using the updated sender cleanup call and signaling completion so waiters are notified during cleanup.
intent_record.what: The call to batadv_tp_sender_cleanup was changed from taking two arguments, bat_priv and tp_vars, to taking only tp_vars, and a new call to complete(&tp_vars->finished) was added immediately before returning in the failed kthread startup cleanup path.
intent_record.how: On kthread startup failure, the cleanup routine is now invoked with its updated signature and the finished completion is explicitly signaled before returning, allowing any waiters on tp_vars->finished to be released instead of potentially remaining blocked after the failure path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize tp_vars->finished when starting a throughput test so later completion-based synchronization works correctly.
intent_record.what: A call to init_completion(&tp_vars->finished) was added in batadv_tp_start() immediately after init_waitqueue_head(&tp_vars->more_bytes), initializing the finished completion object in tp_vars during startup.
intent_record.how: This ensures the finished completion is properly initialized before any runtime use, preventing undefined behavior when code later waits for or signals that completion and enabling correct synchronization for the throughput test lifecycle.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor receiver shutdown to use batadv_tp_list_detach() for centralized TP list removal and bookkeeping.
intent_record.what: The code in batadv_tp_receiver_shutdown() replaces an inline sequence that acquired tp_list_lock, removed tp_vars from the tp list with hlist_del_rcu(), released the lock, dropped the list reference with batadv_tp_vars_put(tp_vars), and decremented bat_priv->tp_num, with a single call to batadv_tp_list_detach(tp_vars).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the shutdown path now performs transport-protocol list detachment through a shared helper instead of open-coded steps, preserving the detach actions while centralizing the removal, reference drop, and counter update logic in one routine.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add batadv_tp_stop_all() to safely cancel and drain all active throughput meter sessions during teardown.
intent_record.what: A new function, batadv_tp_stop_all(struct batadv_priv *bat_priv), was added. It locks bat_priv->tp_list_lock, iterates over bat_priv->tp_list, bounds the collected entries by BATADV_TP_MAX_NUM with WARN_ON_ONCE, acquires temporary references with kref_get_unless_zero, stores matching batadv_tp_vars pointers in a local array, unlocks the list, then processes each saved session by role: for BATADV_TP_SENDER it calls batadv_tp_sender_shutdown(..., BATADV_TP_REASON_CANCEL), wakes tp_var->more_bytes, and waits for tp_var->finished; for BATADV_TP_RECEIVER it detaches the entry from the list, shuts down its timer with timer_shutdown_sync, conditionally drops an extra reference, and finally drops the temporary reference for every saved entry. The function ends with synchronize_net().
intent_record.how: This adds a bulk shutdown path for all active throughput meter sessions associated with a mesh instance. At runtime it safely snapshots the current session list under lock, prevents use-after-free by taking references before releasing the lock, cancels sender sessions and waits for their completion, removes receiver sessions and synchronously stops their timers, then waits for pending network-side activity to quiesce. This enables clean teardown of all in-flight tp_meter sessions and avoids leaving running workers or timers behind.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a public batadv_tp_stop_all() API to allow callers to stop all throughput meter sessions for a batadv instance.
intent_record.what: A new function declaration, `void batadv_tp_stop_all(struct batadv_priv *bat_priv);`, was added to the header alongside the existing throughput meter API declarations.
intent_record.how: This exposes a new interface for stopping all throughput meter activity associated with a `batadv_priv` instance, allowing other translation units to call it at runtime where previously no such public declaration existed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the completion header so the file can use Linux completion APIs without missing declarations or compile errors.
intent_record.what: A new header include line, `#include <linux/completion.h>`, was added to the existing list of Linux kernel header includes.
intent_record.how: This makes completion-related declarations and APIs available to the compilation unit, allowing use of completion synchronization primitives or resolving build issues caused by missing completion definitions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a completion object to batadv_tp_vars so code can synchronize on sender thread exit.
intent_record.what: A new field named `finished` of type `struct completion` was added to `struct batadv_tp_vars`, along with a comment documenting it as a completion signaled when a sender thread exits.
intent_record.how: This extends the test parameter/state structure so runtime code can track and signal sender-thread termination via a kernel completion object, enabling synchronization with thread exit where this structure is used.

Add a public batadv_tp_stop_all() API to allow callers to stop all throughput meter sessions for a batadv instance.

Centralizing TP list removal during receiver shutdown directly concerns the lifetime and teardown of tp_meter sessions in bat_priv->tp_list, which is a key part of the root cause involving sessions remaining active while the mesh interface is being freed.

The root cause is that tp_meter sessions and their threads outlived the mesh interface and continued using bat_priv during teardown. Adding batadv_tp_stop_all() to cancel and drain all active throughput meter sessions during teardown directly addresses that lifetime/synchronization issue.

The root cause is that throughput meter sessions were not stopped when the mesh interface was being torn down. Adding a public batadv_tp_stop_all() API directly enables callers to terminate all tp_meter sessions for a batadv instance, addressing the missing lifetime tie-in between tp sessions and bat_priv teardown.

candidates.rationale: Mesh teardown proceeded with normal cleanup but did not stop or drain active throughput-meter sessions first, leaving tp_list entries and sender activity alive against a deactivating bat_priv.
This teardown step continued freeing mesh-related state without first synchronizing and terminating TP sessions, enabling concurrent use of bat_priv during destruction.
Sender cleanup did not wait for sender-thread completion; cleanup could detach/free session state while other teardown paths or the sender thread still referenced the same bat_priv/tp_vars.
Using non-synchronous delayed-work cancellation allowed finish_work to remain in flight during cleanup, contributing to races where TP activity survived or ran concurrently with mesh teardown.

The session was removed from tp_list, but without a higher-level stop-all and completion-based drain of the sender thread/work, list removal alone did not tie session lifetime to the mesh interface lifetime.

That allowed tp_list sessions and sender activity to outlive the mesh interface lifetime and race with destruction of bat_priv.

This teardown path purged packets but did not terminate throughput-meter sessions or sender threads before later freeing mesh state. The absence of TP shutdown here was part of the lifetime mismatch that left TP activity running against a shutting-down bat_priv.
This cleanup call did not wait for sender-thread completion before proceeding, so tp_vars and bat_priv could still be referenced concurrently by TP sender activity while teardown was advancing.

    batman-adv: throughput meter implementation
    
    The throughput meter module is a simple, kernel-space replacement for
    throughtput measurements tool like iperf and netperf. It is intended to
    approximate TCP behaviour.
    
    It is invoked through batctl: the protocol is connection oriented, with
    cumulative acknowledgment and a dynamic-size
bic_trace_step.reason:
The snippet is sufficient because it contains the full lifetime management for tp_meter sessions/threads/timers. The vulnerable construct is present: tp_meter sessions are attached to `bat_priv->tp_list` and sender activity is started, but there is no mechanism in this code to tie their lifetime to mesh interface teardown or to globally stop all sessions when `bat_priv` is being freed.

Evidence of active sessions bound only by their own local logic:
- New sender sessions are inserted into the global per-mesh list with `hlist_add_head_rcu(&tp_vars->list, &bat_priv->tp_list);` in `batadv_tp_start()`.
- A sender kthread is created in `batadv_tp_start_kthread()` via `kthread_create(batadv_tp_send, tp_vars, ...)` and started with `wake_up_process(kthread);`.
- A sender timer is armed in `batadv_tp_start()` with `setup_timer(&tp_vars->timer, batadv_tp_sender_timeout, (unsigned long)tp_vars);` and then scheduled from `batadv_tp_send()` via `batadv_tp_reset_sender_timer(tp_vars);`.
- A delayed work item is queued in `batadv_tp_send()` with `queue_delayed_work(batadv_event_workqueue, &tp_vars->finish_work, ...)`.

These background activities continue to dereference `tp_vars->bat_priv` / `bat_priv`:
- `batadv_tp_send()` caches `struct batadv_priv *bat_priv = tp_vars->bat_priv;` and later calls helpers using it, then `batadv_tp_sender_end(bat_priv, tp_vars);` and `batadv_tp_sender_cleanup(bat_priv, tp_vars);`.
- `batadv_tp_sender_timeout()` does `struct batadv_priv *bat_priv = tp_vars->bat_priv;` and uses it for logging and behavior.
- Receiver timeout path `batadv_tp_receiver_shutdown()` also does `bat_priv = tp_vars->bat_priv;` and manipulates `tp_vars->bat_priv->tp_list_lock`.

What is missing, matching the root cause:
- There is no check of a mesh-interface shutdown/removal state before starting or continuing sessions.
- There is no function here that walks `bat_priv->tp_list` during mesh teardown to stop sender threads, cancel delayed work, and synchronously drain timers before `bat_priv` can disappear.
- Cleanup only happens on normal per-session completion (`batadv_tp_sender_cleanup()` / `batadv_tp_receiver_shutdown()`), not on mesh lifetime end.

Therefore the code introduces sessions and asynchronous sender/timer/work activity that can outlive the mesh interface lifetime, which is exactly the vulnerable condition described. No fix is present in this function set.

The vulnerable construct is present: tp_meter sessions are tied only to their own sender/receiver logic and are stored on `bat_priv->tp_list`, but there is no mechanism here to stop all sessions when the mesh interface / `bat_priv` is being torn down. Specifically, sender sessions are added to the mesh-global list with `hlist_add_head_rcu(&tp_vars->list, &bat_priv->tp_list);` in `batadv_tp_start()`, and receiver sessions likewise in `batadv_tp_init_recv()`. Sender sessions also spawn an independent kernel thread via `kthread_create(batadv_tp_send, tp_vars, ...)` in `batadv_tp_start_kthread()`, queue delayed work with `queue_delayed_work(..., &tp_vars->finish_work, ...)` in `batadv_tp_send()`, and arm timers with `setup_timer(&tp_vars->timer, batadv_tp_sender_timeout, ...)` / `mod_timer(...)`. Receiver sessions similarly arm timers in `batadv_tp_init_recv()` / `batadv_tp_reset_receiver_timer()`. These asynchronous entities dereference `tp_vars->bat_priv` after creation, for example `struct batadv_priv *bat_priv = tp_vars->bat_priv;` in `batadv_tp_send()` and `batadv_tp_sender_timeout()`, and `bat_priv = tp_vars->bat_priv;` in `batadv_tp_receiver_shutdown()`. There is no code in this file that ties session lifetime to mesh lifetime by taking a mesh-interface reference, checking a shutdown flag, or providing a global teardown routine to flush `bat_priv->tp_list` and stop all associated threads/timers/work before `bat_priv` is freed. Therefore the root cause condition exists: active `tp_list` sessions and sender threads/timers can outlive or race with mesh teardown and use a shutting-down `bat_priv`. No fix is present in this commit version.
